title: Lowest common ancestor in a BST
md:
## The idea

In a BST, smaller values are on the left and larger on the right. So from the root: if **both** values are smaller, the answer is on the left; if both are larger, on the right; otherwise this node is where their paths **split** — the answer.

## Step by step

1. lo = smaller of the two values, hi = larger.
2. cur = root.
3. If hi < cur → go left. If lo > cur → go right.
4. Otherwise return cur.

## Worked example

**Input:** BST [6,2,8,0,4,7,9,null,null,3,5], nodes 3 and 5

| Step | What happens |
|---|---|
| at 6 | both smaller → left |
| at 2 | both larger → right |
| at 4 | 3 ≤ 4 ≤ 5 → split here |

**Result:** node 4

## Cost

O(h) time, O(1) memory.

## The code (C#, compiled and tested against every part of the question)

```csharp
// TreeNode is provided by the starter (Models.cs): int Value; TreeNode Left, Right.

// LeetCode 235 — lowest common ancestor of two nodes in a binary SEARCH tree.
public static class LcaBst {
    public static TreeNode Find(TreeNode root, TreeNode p, TreeNode q) {
        int lo = Math.Min(p.Value, q.Value), hi = Math.Max(p.Value, q.Value);
        TreeNode cur = root;
        while (cur != null) {
            if (hi < cur.Value) cur = cur.Left;          // both are smaller: the split is on the left
            else if (lo > cur.Value) cur = cur.Right;    // both are larger: on the right
            else return cur;                             // they split here (or one of them is here)
        }
        return null;
    }
}
```

## Likely follow-up questions

**Q: What if a node might be missing?**

Verify both exist first (two O(h) searches), then find the split.

**Q: Complexity?**

O(h): O(log n) when balanced, O(n) when skewed.

**Q: Shared state?**

Read-only tree.

**Q: Millions of LCA queries.**

Preprocess with an Euler tour + sparse table (O(1) per query) or binary lifting (O(log n)).
